question.text:
How many interhalogen compounds are not possible?

ICl, IBr, BrI, ClBr3,ClF3,BrCl5,BrI5,ICl3,IF7

solution.text: BrI,  <math><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></math>  are not possible as  <math><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">′</mi></mrow></msubsup></math>  type of interhalogen compounds exist only when X = less E.N. and larger size while  <math><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">′</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo></math>  more E.N. and small size.
